aboutme.title: I'm Daniel Mihaylov
aboutme.subtitle: I'm a UX/UI Designer and Front-end Developer, with a degree in Industrial Design from the Technical University of Varna, where I'm now studying for my master's degree. Currently, I work as an E-Commerce Developer at NUTRIKAL, building custom websites for food-supplement brands from design systems to production frontends. I use Figma, Vue.js, TypeScript, REST APIs, SVG and HTML5 Canvas to create responsive, accessible interfaces.

job-1.description: Building fully custom websites for food-supplement brands, from design systems to production frontends. Own the visual language, including colour palettes, typography and reusable components. Build responsive frontends with Vue.js and TypeScript, consuming REST APIs based on OpenAPI 3.0. Built an in-house content tool with a drag-and-drop editor, a publishing pipeline and live updates over WebSockets and SSE. Create interactive visualizations with SVG and HTML5 Canvas, and prototype accessible components in Figma for authentication-aware flows.

job-2.description: Designed web pages focused on clear structure, usability and a memorable experience. Created wireframes, prototypes and high-fidelity mockups in Figma and Sketch, conducted user research, and applied UX principles to create intuitive, accessible interfaces. Built and maintained a shared design system and component library. Created visual content for websites, online stores, email newsletters and digital campaigns, collaborating with developers, the marketing team and the project manager.

job-3.description: As Interior designer at Lazur, I was responsible for creating functional and aesthetically pleasing interior spaces that met the needs and preferences of clients. My duties included conceptualizing and developing design ideas, selecting materials, colors, and furnishings, and collaborating with architects and contractors to ensure the successful execution of projects. I also created detailed drawings and 3D models to visualize design concepts and presented them to clients for approval. Additionally, I stayed updated on industry trends and incorporated sustainable design practices into my work.

job-4.description: As a Graphic Design intern at Wild Art, I assisted in creating visual content for various marketing materials, including social media graphics, brochures, and advertisements. I collaborated with the design team to develop concepts and layouts that aligned with the company's branding guidelines. My responsibilities included photo editing, typography selection, and preparing files for print and digital distribution. This internship provided me with valuable hands-on experience in a professional design environment and helped me enhance my skills in graphic design software such as Adobe Photoshop and Illustrator.

projectOne.title: EVL-Studio
projectOne.description: EVL-Studio is a e-commerce websiite that will sell posters prints. It will be built with Hydrogen framework and Shopify. The design is modern and minimalistic, with a focus on showcasing the products in an elegant way. The website will have a user-friendly interface, making it easy for customers to browse and purchase the posters.

projectTwo.title: Vanilla Design
projectTwo.description: Vanilla design is a modern and minimalist print shop website designed to provide users with a seamless experience in browsing and purchasing high-quality printed materials. The project has Low-fi and Hi-fi wireframes, user flows, style guide and complete UX/UI design. The design is slick and light, with a focus on simplicity and elegance.

projectThree.title: Vestimenta Lux
projectThree.description: I’ve been working on a fully interactive e-commerce prototype for luxury clothing, and I’m thrilled to finally showcase it! This project is designed to offer a seamless shopping experience with elegance and functionality at its core.

projectFour.description: Jekoni is a business specializing in metal constructions, including industrial halls and bespoke metal building projects.
